verses.note: Abram's refusal is faith in action. God had promised to bless him (12:2), and he will not let anyone else, least of all Sodom, take the credit. The next chapter answers him at once, with God promising to be his very great reward (15:1).
The Bible's first explicit statement of faith is trust in a person who has made a promise, not assent to an idea. Abram has nothing but God's word, and he rests on it.
Sarah laughed in doubt and now laughs in joy. Hebrews 11:11 still counts her among the faithful, which shows that Scripture measures faith by where it rests at last, not by whether it ever wavered.
